item: W16 a memory that disagrees with an instruction file reaches one of three verdicts
coordinateUnit: zero-based UTF-16, left-closed/end-exclusive, over the decoded module text
readAs: inert data; no recovered entrypoint was executed

facts.name: the reconcile procedure, as prompt text
facts.text: For each memory that captures feedback or project conventions (the feedback/project types, where tagged), check whether it contradicts a CLAUDE.md instruction on the same topic: the memory is stale and is deleted or rewritten because CLAUDE.md is the maintained, checked-in source; or CLAUDE.md may be stale and the memory is annotated "contradicts CLAUDE.md - verify which is current" and listed for the user, with CLAUDE.md not edited during a dream; or it is not a conflict and the memory stays. A feedback memory's "Why: the user corrected me" framing is not evidence that it is newer than CLAUDE.md.

facts.name: the dream prompt that quotes it
the gates, with their defaults
facts.note: 24 hours since the last consolidation and 5 sessions since, both read from a config flag that falls back to those numbers

facts.name: the runner
facts.note: reads the last-consolidated stamp, lists the sessions touched since, refuses to run when a permission rule would block memory writes, takes a consolidation lock, runs a forked subagent with a restricted tool set, then settles what that run wrote

facts.name: the two memory-item states that skip a run
facts.note: reported by name with their own notices; both are already covered here on the write path, as an unreadable entry error and the expected_sha256 conflict

facts.name: the read-only tool constraint for the run
facts.text: Shell access is restricted to read-only commands (ls, find, grep, cat, stat, wc, head, tail, and similar) plus deleting .md files inside the memory directory (outside protected subdirectories like .git or agents; rm takes no flags except -f).

portedInvariant: A memory that captures feedback or a project convention can describe a different procedure than the project's instruction files for the same task, and the disagreement is decided rather than left implicit: the memory is stale and goes, the instruction file may be stale and the memory is annotated and surfaced, or there is no conflict and the memory stays.

wiring.note: the constant is interpolated into the reconcile paragraph of AUTO_MEMORY_INSTRUCTIONS (src/auto-memory.ts:15), which src/agent.ts:88 appends to the system prompt when auto-memory is on and both read tools exist, so the literal and the text cannot drift apart

ownedDecisions: The rule lands on the maintenance instructions rather than a background pass, because this runtime has no unattended consolidation run; the instruction-file set is named as the two files this runtime loads.
The annotation is an exported constant quoted into the text, so the literal a person greps for and the text the model reads cannot drift apart.
The recovered em dash is written as a hyphen: every file in this project is ASCII. The wording is otherwise unchanged.

"Do not edit CLAUDE.md during a dream" becomes conditional on the user, because maintenance here happens in a conversation where editing an instruction file can be exactly what the user asked for; the may-be-stale case tells the user instead of editing.
"List it in your summary" becomes "tell the user in your reply": there is no summary artifact here.
The "where tagged" qualifier is kept, because the local store has no type field - types live in the memory body's metadata.
notPorted: The whole dream runner: the hour and session gates, the 600-second throttle, the consolidation lock, the forked subagent with its read-only tool list, the write-permission pre-check, the settle and capped-write reconciliation, the task registration and the completion notice. This runtime has no scheduled or background agent run, so porting the runner would mean building that surface first.

The two memory-item skip states as runner states: an unreadable entry already raises memory: entry contains invalid UTF-8 and a record that moved already raises memory: SHA-256 conflict; read the current document before updating (src/memory.ts:103, :321), so no rule was missing.
The read-only shell constraint list, which exists only to bound the forked run.

added: the annotation constant equals the ASCII literal and appears quoted inside the instructions; the three verdicts are each identifiable by their distinguishing phrase; the instruction file is not edited by maintenance the user did not ask for and the user is told instead; a correction is not evidence of recency; the two instruction files this runtime loads are named; and the pre-existing rules (expected_sha256, untrusted data, precedence, no separate extraction call) all still hold

cliSmoke.reason: the deliverable is prompt text that reaches the model plus the constant it quotes, and the case asserts both directly; a CLI run would show the same bytes in a system prompt without reaching anything new.

regressions: None. The reconcile paragraph is appended to the instructions; no existing line changed, and the case asserts the pre-existing rules still hold.
limitations: The judgment is prompt text, so what actually happens when a model reconciles a memory is not observed here - the ported artifact is the instruction, and the case asserts the instruction, not a model's compliance with it.
The instruction-file set is the two files this runtime loads; the recovered text names one.
No unattended consolidation run exists here, so the gates, the lock and the settle behaviour are recorded rather than exercised.
